market.h2: How Wynwood picks where to eat
paragraphsHtml: Wynwood grew around art, not food. The Wynwood Walls opened in 2009, and the restaurants, breweries and bars followed the crowds that came to see the murals. That still shapes your business: many of the people on NW 2nd Avenue came for the neighborhood, not for you, and they decide where to eat on the spot.

That decision happens on a phone. Someone a block away searches “tacos near me,” taps the map, looks at your photos and your last few posts, and chooses in seconds. If your listing looks stale or your food photos are dark, they walk to the next place with a line.

The calendar matters too. Art Basel week in early December and Miami Music Week in March bring waves of visitors who are already in the neighborhood and hungry, while the quieter weeks lean harder on locals. A plan that knows what is coming fills more seats than one that reacts.

needs.h2: What a Wynwood restaurant needs most

items.title: Short video that holds its own next to the murals
items.body: Your guests are already filming everything around them. Reels and TikToks of your plates, your bar and your room give them a reason to pick you, and give your own guests something worth sharing.

items.title: A Google listing built for walk-ins
items.body: Your Google Business Profile (the listing that shows on Google Maps) is the first thing a nearby searcher sees. Current hours, fresh photos, a working menu link and recent reviews decide whether they walk over.

items.title: A plan for event weeks
items.body: Basel and Music Week bring people who are already here and looking for somewhere to eat. Content, ads and a menu plan lined up a few weeks ahead let you capture that crowd instead of watching it pass.

items.title: Everything in English and Spanish
items.body: Wynwood draws locals, tourists and a big Latin crowd. Captions, review replies and ads in both languages reach guests that a one-language feed misses.

plan.h2: What we would do for a Wynwood restaurant

items.title: Social media and on-site content
items.bodyHtml: We shoot food photography and short video at your restaurant, then plan, post and manage your Instagram and TikTok so your page always looks current when someone checks it from the sidewalk. That is how our restaurant social media and content service works.

items.title: Google Maps and local search
items.bodyHtml: We clean up your Google Business Profile, keep photos and hours current, and build a steady flow of reviews so you show up when people nearby search. It is the core of our restaurant SEO and Google Business Profile work.

items.title: A website that works on the sidewalk
items.bodyHtml: Many Wynwood visitors check you on a phone while standing outside. We build fast, bilingual, mobile-first sites with your menu and booking or ordering one tap away. See our restaurant website design.

items.title: Ads timed to the calendar
items.bodyHtml: Google and Meta ads aimed at people near Wynwood, pushed harder around the big event weeks, with tracking on calls, reservations and orders. Nothing launches until tracking is verified. Here is how our restaurant Google and Meta ads are built.

shoots.body: We come to your restaurant and shoot there: plated dishes, drinks, the room and the people who run it. Shoots are scheduled around your service so the camera never gets in the way of a rush, and food close-ups are usually done before doors open. The same in-house team that plans your content shoots it, with nothing handed off to a contractor, and one shoot typically gives us 4 to 6 weeks of content across your platforms. Planning starts with a strategy call hosted by Juan Hernandez, our founder, so we agree on what to capture before anyone picks up a camera.

pricing.bodyHtml: Most restaurants invest $1,500 to $5,000 per month for a coordinated program across social, Google and ads. A new website is a one-time $1,500 (Website Build) or $2,000 (Integrated Website Build, which adds POS menu sync, reservations and ordering). Ad management comes with no long-term contract. Not sure where to start? The free Social Media & Website Grader scores your restaurant against nearby competitors.

faqs.q: Do you work with restaurants in Wynwood?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with restaurants, bars and cafes across Miami and South Florida, Wynwood included. Our work close by includes Shimuja Ramen in Downtown Miami, featured in our case studies.

faqs.q: Can you shoot content while we are open?
faqs.a: Yes. If you want a full room on camera, we plan the shoot so we stay out of your staff's way. Food and drink close-ups usually work best before service, when the kitchen can plate for the camera.

faqs.q: Do you make content in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. Our team is bilingual, so captions, review replies, ads and your website can run in English, Spanish or both.

faqs.q: How should I market my restaurant around Art Basel?
faqs.a: Start several weeks ahead: content that shows what is special that week, ads aimed at visitors nearby, and accurate hours on Google. The goal is to capture a crowd that is already in the neighborhood.

faqs.q: How much does restaurant marketing cost?
faqs.a: Most restaurants invest $1,500 to $5,000 per month for a coordinated program. A website build is a one-time $1,500 or $2,000.
